opus-5.5.text:
I think it comes down to a few things.

First, the problem itself is really exciting. We're working on 3D generative AI, which is still a very young field. In 2D, images and video, a lot of progress has already happened. 3D is harder. The data is scarce, the representations are complicated, and the quality bar from artists and game developers is very high. So there are a lot of genuinely unsolved problems. If you're someone who likes hard technical challenges, this is a place where you can do work that actually moves the frontier, not just tune something that already works.

Second, it's a place where research and product are very tightly connected. Coming from an academic background myself, at MIT working on computer graphics and Taichi, I've always cared about building things people actually use. At Meshy, when someone on the team improves a model or a pipeline, it can reach millions of users quickly. You get real feedback from game developers, 3D printing hobbyists, artists, educators. That loop is very satisfying, and I think it makes people grow fast.

Third, the team. We try to keep it small and very high talent density. Everyone has a lot of ownership. There isn't much bureaucracy, so if you have a good idea you can just go build it. We value people who are self-driven, curious, and honest, people who care more about getting the right answer than about being right. I think that kind of culture makes work more fun, because you're surrounded by people you can learn from every day.

And finally, I think it's simply a great time to be here. Generative AI is changing how content gets created, and 3D is one of the last big frontiers. Being an early part of that, helping define what the tools look like for the next decade, is a rare opportunity. So if someone wants to work on something meaningful, technically deep, and with real impact, I think Meshy is a really good place for that.

r002.rationale: The candidate does not compare narrow tasks at a big company with larger-scale computing work at Meshy.

fable-5.1.text:
Thanks for having me. I think Meshy is a great place to work for a few reasons.

First, the problem itself. We're building AI tools that let anyone create 3D content from text or images, and 3D is one of the hardest, most under-served areas in generative AI. It's not a solved problem like text or even 2D images. Every week we're pushing on things nobody has figured out yet, like geometry quality, texturing, rigging, animation, and making it all fast enough that a real artist or game developer actually wants to use it. If you like hard technical problems with a very visible payoff, that's genuinely exciting.

Second, the people. A lot of our team comes from a deep graphics and systems background. My own path goes back to Taichi, the programming language I built at MIT for high-performance graphics and physics simulation, and many of the folks here share that mindset of caring about both the research side and the engineering side. You end up surrounded by people who can talk about diffusion models in the morning and GPU memory layouts in the afternoon. That density of talent makes everyone better.

Third, the feedback loop. We have millions of users, and they tell us very quickly whether something works. There's nothing abstract about it. You ship a model improvement, and the next day you can see what people made with it. That's incredibly motivating for engineers and researchers who want their work to matter outside a paper.

And finally, I'd say ownership. We're still a relatively small team for the scale of what we're doing, so people get real responsibility early. If you have an idea and can execute, you can shape the product. I think that combination of a hard, unsolved problem, strong colleagues, fast user feedback, and real ownership is pretty rare, and it's why I think people enjoy working here.
